triplets.head: Sennheiser
triplets.tail: Famously pokes fun at celebrity endorsements in advertising; uses professional artist collaborations and community-based Consumer Ambassador Program

triplets.head: Sony
triplets.tail: Runs product collaborations (Olivia Rodrigo for LinkBuds earbuds, Post Malone for ULT WEAR campaign) and social media Audio Ambassadors, but no formally titled global celebrity ambassador for over-ear headphones

triplets.head: AKG
triplets.tail: Previously collaborated with Quincy Jones on N90Q headphone (2015) as product design collaboration; no current celebrity endorsement program

triplets.head: Beyerdynamic
triplets.tail: Historically featured Phil Collins in ads; Emiliano Cyrus served as regional China ambassador for e-sports headphones (2023-2025); no current global celebrity endorser

triplets.head: Audio-Technica
triplets.tail: Selena Gomez was an endorser in 2011 (long ended); now focuses on professional artist communities and creator programs

triplets.head: Focal
triplets.tail: Focuses on professional partnerships and audiophile credibility rather than celebrity marketing

triplets.head: Shure
triplets.tail: Adam Levine fronted AONIC 50 launch campaign in 2020 (one-time campaign, not ongoing ambassadorship)

triplets.head: Grado
triplets.tail: Explicitly eschews celebrity endorsements; one-off collaboration with Elijah Wood on limited-edition whiskey-barrel headphones (2013); relies on word-of-mouth

triplets.head: STAX
triplets.tail: Ultra-niche electrostatic headphone manufacturer with no celebrity marketing

triplets.head: Audeze
triplets.tail: Collaborates with Grammy-winning engineer/producer Manny Marroquin (MM-Series headphones); targets audio professionals
